findings.summary: landingMarkers cut each clause from one branch token to the NEXT one, so the last-named branch in the bullet took every remaining word of it - 1639 of 2363 characters, 69%. Measured on the shipped parser against the shipped handoff, lane/native-routing-271 came out carrying c8366609 (the fork point of two OTHER branches) and PR #275 (a different lane's PR).
findings.why: That lane carries 3 commits and is not an ancestor of origin/main, so neither rule A nor rule D reaches its marker, and --is-ancestor lane/native-routing-271 c8366609 exits 1 anyway, so verifyMergeRef would return false and rule D would report 'that reference landed something else'. Nothing was suppressed. The reason to fix it is that the fail-OPEN version is one sentence away: delete the 'diverge at c8366609' phrase upstream and the same clause yields a PR-only marker, which unmarkedLanding accepts without verifying anything, and the lane is permanently excused from A and D on prose that was never about it.
findings.fix: CLAUSE_END = /[.;]\s|\s\u00b7\s/ stops a clause at the next branch name, the end of its sentence, or the middle dot the list already uses, whichever comes first. Plus the matching doc fix, because 'those two LANDED (PR #275 . PR #273)' was one sentence marking two names, which is the defect rule D's own error text names. The doc fix ALONE would not have been enough: with each name marked but the clause still unbounded, native-routing-271 goes from {c8366609, 275} to {c8366609, 273} - the right PR wearing the wrong SHA, which is the failure mode that survives review.
findings.guard: Three pins added, per bug -> guard: trailing prose after the last name marks nothing; a real marker survives while the sentence after it is refused (a borrowed SHA is a wrong ANSWER, not a refusal); and a sibling entry across the middle dot is a different entry. handoff-worktree-truth went 11 -> 14.
